first.rationale: Simplifying onboarding directly addresses the 4% completion decline and may also recover activation, with two inherited results indicating durable activation, adoption, and time-to-value gains. Promotional pricing responds to the competitor but carries documented 30-day retention risk, conflicting with sustainable long-term qualified revenue.

final.rationale: Run a guarded simplification of the onboarding flow, prioritizing fewer steps and faster time-to-value rather than indiscriminately removing signup qualification fields. The verified onboarding experiment improved completion by 13%, shortened time-to-value by 2.1 days, and increased 30-day retention by 3%, directly addressing both current declines while supporting sustainable revenue. Signup simplification also lifted SMB activation and qualified revenue, but its 1% retention decline and limited segment replication warrant downstream retention monitoring. Promotional pricing is not preferred because its known retention harm conflicts with the long-term objective.
